- **STBL**: A string table resource (type 0x220557DA): a list of 32-bit keys with UTF-8 text, one table per language and pack. ([7.01](7.01-ui-dialogs-tutorials.md))
- **story arc**: A tuned story (pregnancy, adoption, accidental death, career change, relationship change, move in, move out) attached to one Sim, a group of Sims or a household, made of one or more chapters. ([4.02](4.02-story-progression-townies.md))
- **story chapter**: One step of a story arc: preconditions, loot, actions and the weighted link to the next chapter. ([4.02](4.02-story-progression-townies.md))
- **story discovery**: The text a Sim reads at the mailbox ("Check Recent Neighborhood Stories"): one random past story chapter from the last five days, removed from history once shown. ([4.02](4.02-story-progression-townies.md))
- **story progression**: The background system that changes the lives of unplayed Sims and households: daily story arcs plus older periodic actions such as culling. ([4.02](4.02-story-progression-townies.md))
- **story progression pass**: One entry of the daily seeding list: a demographic measure, bands of chance and count, and the arcs it may start. ([4.02](4.02-story-progression-townies.md))
- **story progression rule**: A player-facing switch (for example MoveIn or AccidentalDeath) that an arc requires; checked against the save's rule sets. ([4.02](4.02-story-progression-townies.md))
- **Stray**: A wild cat or dog that wanders open streets for up to 360 Sim minutes and can be adopted free once a Sim is its friend. ([3.12](3.12-pets-horses.md))
- **street**: Tuning record for one world file (one loaded neighbourhood); names the open street director, civic policy provider, townie target and optional travel or vacation lot. ([2.06](2.06-worlds-regions-travel.md))
- **street civic policy**: A StreetCivicPolicy snippet that a street can enact by vote; it runs a list of street effects while enacted. ([2.07](2.07-neighbourhood-systems.md))
- **street effect**: A snippet (layer, loot, map overlay, weather, shut-off, plex exterior, situation) that a policy or eco state turns on and off. ([2.07](2.07-neighbourhood-systems.md))
- **street weather effect**: StreetWeatherEffect: an EP09 civic-policy effect that sends a sky or weather channel value straight to the client. ([2.04](2.04-weather-seasons-ground.md))
- **string table**: An STBL resource (type 0x220557DA): a list of 32-bit string ids and UTF-8 texts for one pack and one language. ([8.01](8.01-package-files.md))
- **sub-situation**: A situation created and owned by another situation; it reports its end to the owner, is destroyed with it and is not saved on its own. ([4.01](4.01-situations-npcs.md))
- **sub-venue**: A venue a variable venue can switch to, such as a community lot's garden or market, or an auditorium's graduation. ([2.01](2.01-lots-venues-rooms.md))
- **subaction autonomy**: The SubActionAutonomy mode: picks mixers inside a running interaction or offered by a buff; runs at every state above DISABLED. ([3.04](3.04-autonomy.md))
- **subroot**: A rig joint b__subroot__N that places part N; a Subroot record lists the bone names a part owns, suffixed with its index ([2.02](2.02-objects-states-wear.md))
- **success modifier**: A buff field in percentage points that raises or lowers the Sim's chance of success on interactions. ([3.07](3.07-personality-feelings.md))
- **SuccessChance**: A base percent times tested multipliers, capped at 100%; used by loot ops and pass/fail outcomes. ([0.04](0.04-tests-loot-effects.md))
- **summary sign**: The DynamicSignView of type SCENARIO (op 320) shown when a scenario ends without an outcome, listing completed goals and time spent. ([4.05](4.05-scenarios-moments.md))
- **sun exposure**: commodity_Vampire_SunExposure; it falls while a vampire is dying in the sun and its failure kills the vampire. ([3.11](3.11-occults.md))
- **sun out**: Day time in a world that provides sunlight, with no shading weather (TimeService.is_sun_out). ([2.05](2.05-sky-and-moon.md))
- **sunrise time**: The tuned time of day (Region.sunrise_time, default 6:00) at which gameplay day starts in a world. ([2.05](2.05-sky-and-moon.md))
- **sunset time**: The tuned time of day (Region.sunset_time, default 20:00) at which gameplay day ends in a world. ([2.05](2.05-sky-and-moon.md))
- **Super failure**: The worst discipline outcome: the pet becomes Vengeful and the Sim-to-pet relationship drops sharply. ([3.12](3.12-pets-horses.md))
- **Super Green Thumb**: A trait whose Sims mark plants they water; marked plants grow twice as fast, dry five times slower and get bugs ten times slower. ([6.02](6.02-gardening-fishing-collecting.md))
- **super interaction**: A long-lived activity (sit, cook, sleep, talk) that enters the Sim's SIState and can host mixers. ([3.05](3.05-interactions-postures-routing.md))
- **super speed 3**: The fastest speed (x36 by default), granted only while every Sim in the household is doing something that asks for it and nothing on the lot blocks it. ([1.01](1.01-time-scheduling-loading.md))
- **supports lunar cycle**: Region flag; when False no lunar effects reach Sims there and the client is told to skip moon-dependent environment changes. ([2.05](2.05-sky-and-moon.md))
- **suppression group**: A named cap on a family of notifications, counted per save or per tick, with a limit and a fallback (nothing, another notification, or a tested one). ([7.01](7.01-ui-dialogs-tutorials.md))
- **surplus**: A utility meter above 0.75 (sell value minus 0.25); a utility with surplus works even with shut-off reasons. ([5.01](5.01-money-bills-rewards.md))
- **surprise holiday**: One of eight EP05 pop-up holidays scored weekly on Monday; it starts at 06:00 on its weekday with no pre-day. ([4.04](4.04-events-holidays-festivals.md))
- **swatch**: One colour variant of a garment or hair; each swatch is its own CASP sharing the meshes of the others. ([3.02](3.02-cas-sculpting-parts.md))
- **swimwear change depth**: Water depth on a planned route past which a Sim changes outfit for the tuned reason (EnterOceanWater) before it starts walking. ([2.06](2.06-worlds-regions-travel.md))
- **SwitchOccultElement**: An interaction element that switches a Sim's form; live users are swim and bath postures and diving-board jumps. ([3.11](3.11-occults.md))
- **Symptom**: A sickness tuning record describing one sign of an illness: it adds buffs and statistics while the illness lasts, and diagnosis (by the vet, for pets) reveals symptoms one by one. ([3.12](3.12-pets-horses.md), [3.13](3.13-health-luck-fame.md))
## T

- **table set**: The native name for the SimData DATA container: a header, a table directory, schemas and rows. ([8.02](8.02-tuning-formats.md))
- **tag**
  1. A value of the Tag enum that labels objects, interactions, situations and other records for filtering. ([0.03](0.03-tuning-system.md))
  2. Distributor tag: a distributor id opened while a clip-event handler runs; ops created then wait on that tag so the client can release them at the event. ([3.06](3.06-animation.md))
- **tag category**: A value of the TagCategory enum that groups tags. ([0.03](0.03-tuning-system.md))
- **tan level**: The Sim's suntan state (TanLevel): NO_TAN 0, DEEP 1, SUNBURNED 2, sent to the client with the outfit parts that leave tan lines. ([3.01](3.01-create-a-sim.md))
- **tardy request**: A request still unfulfilled 30 Sim minutes after submission; the job's no_show_action decides what happens. ([4.01](4.01-situations-npcs.md))
- **tattoo tracker**: Per-Sim record (EP18) of tattoo quality, sentiment, dedicated Sim and layers for each tattoo body type. ([6.01](6.01-crafting-cooking.md))
- **tax level**: A neighbourhood's EP21 tax setting (Normal, VeryLow, Low, High, VeryHigh) that the bills module turns into a bill multiplier. ([6.03](6.03-pack-systems.md))
- **TDESC**: Tuning description: the developer schema of every tunable, not shipped with the game. ([0.03](0.03-tuning-system.md))
- **telegraph effect**: A lunar effect at 07:00 that announces the phase's main effect due later that day. ([2.05](2.05-sky-and-moon.md))
- **telemetry filter rule**: A (priority, module/group/hook prefix, fields, action) rule that decides whether Python passes a hook on; COLLECT passes, DROP stops. ([1.04](1.04-debug-cheats-telemetry.md))
- **telemetry group**: The four-letter tag of a TelemetryWriter (for example CHTS for cheats, CLCK for the clock). ([1.04](1.04-debug-cheats-telemetry.md))
- **telemetry hook**: One telemetry event, written with begin_hook(writer, HOOK) and committed to native _telemetry.log_event when the with block ends. ([1.04](1.04-debug-cheats-telemetry.md))
- **teleport cost**: Statistic and amount a teleport style takes; without one, cost tests on that style always fail. ([2.06](2.06-worlds-regions-travel.md))
- **teleport cost multiplier**: Buff value that scales a Sim's teleport cost; all active multipliers are multiplied together. ([2.06](2.06-worlds-regions-travel.md))
- **teleport style**: A way of moving that replaces walking with a vanish and reappear (bat, mist, wolf, witch, basic and others). ([2.06](2.06-worlds-regions-travel.md))
- **temperament**: One of 22 werewolf traits; a werewolf may hold one per rank, up to four. ([3.11](3.11-occults.md))
- **temperature word**: The Temperature enum on a weather event: Freezing, Cold, Cool, Warm, Hot or Burning; every melt, thaw, frost and drying rate is set per word. ([2.04](2.04-weather-seasons-ground.md))
- **template affordance**: An extra interaction a Sim offers for a while after a template interaction starts, such as discipline. ([4.02](4.02-story-progression-townies.md))
- **template chooser**: A weighted list that picks which Sim template a filter uses when it creates a Sim. ([4.02](4.02-story-progression-townies.md))
- **temple**: A GP06 (Jungle Adventure) lot in the jungle built from one of five house descriptions: an entrance and a chain of rooms closed by gates, with a rare chest in the last room. ([6.03](6.03-pack-systems.md))
- **temple gate**: An object tagged Func_Temple_Gate between two temple rooms; it belongs to the lower-numbered room and is locked for every Sim until the room's puzzle is solved. ([6.03](6.03-pack-systems.md))
- **temple lock commodity**: commodity_PathObstacle_TempleLock, which keeps the jungle's temple entrance blocked after a reset until it decays to 0. ([6.03](6.03-pack-systems.md))
- **temple room**: One plex of a temple lot; room 0 is the entrance (outside every plex), rooms 1 and up are plexes 1 and up. ([6.03](6.03-pack-systems.md))
- **temple state**: The jungle open street director's record of the current temple: needs reset, reset, in progress or complete. ([6.03](6.03-pack-systems.md))
- **tenant application list**: EP15's list of 15 applicant households (homeless households, premade and random templates) shown when a rental unit needs tenants. ([2.01](2.01-lots-venues-rooms.md))
- **terminator**: A scenario test registered on the event manager that ends a phase (phase terminator) or the whole scenario (scenario terminator) when it passes. ([4.05](4.05-scenarios-moments.md))
- **terrain tag**: A ground material under a point (grass, sand, wood deck and so on) used by placement and tests. ([2.03](2.03-build-buy-placement.md))
- **test**: A tuned yes-or-no check (a BaseTest) that names the participants it needs and returns a TestResult. ([0.04](0.04-tests-loot-effects.md))
- **test event**: A TestEvent value (158 of them) that a system fires through the event manager when something happens. ([0.04](0.04-tests-loot-effects.md))
- **test profile**: An automation-only record of count, resolve time and test time per test set or loot, per resolver and key. ([1.03](1.03-performance-lod.md))
- **test set**: A TunableTestSet: an OR of AND groups; the first group whose tests all pass wins, and an empty set passes. ([0.04](0.04-tests-loot-effects.md))
- **test set snippet**: A TestSetInstance, a reusable test set tuned as a SNIPPET and referenced with test_set_reference; it can invert its result. ([0.04](0.04-tests-loot-effects.md))
- **test-based score**: A TestBasedScore instance: the sum of the scores of every passing test entry, compared to a threshold by TestBasedScoreThresholdTest and used, for example, to choose a social's outcome. ([0.04](0.04-tests-loot-effects.md), [3.08](3.08-relationships-socials.md))
- **tested game effect modifier**: A game effect modifier that applies only if its test set passes once, when the buff is added. ([0.04](0.04-tests-loot-effects.md))
- **tested sum**: A base value plus the sum, or the largest, of the modifiers whose tests pass. ([0.03](0.03-tuning-system.md))
- **testingcheats**: The Live command that switches Cheat commands on or off for the account by setting CheatService.cheats_enabled; on consoles it first asks for confirmation. ([0.02](0.02-architecture.md), [1.04](1.04-debug-cheats-telemetry.md))
- **TestResult**: The result of a test: truthy or falsy, with a debug reason, an optional tooltip and icon. ([0.04](0.04-tests-loot-effects.md))
- **TestResultNumeric**: A TestResult that also carries current and goal values, used for objective progress. ([0.04](0.04-tests-loot-effects.md))
- **text node**: In packed XML, a node with neither attributes nor children; its string is the text of its parent element. ([8.02](8.02-tuning-formats.md))
- **Thirst**: Vampire plasma, commodity_Motive_Visible_Vampire_Thirst, decaying 0.1042 a minute. ([3.11](3.11-occults.md))
- **threshold action**: Action run when diagnosis passes a threshold: discover_symptom, discover_sickness, rule_out_treatment or apply_loots. ([3.13](3.13-health-luck-fame.md))
- **thrift store inventory**: The daily set of CAS parts the EP12 thrift store offers, rebuilt every morning. ([4.03](4.03-groups-factions.md))
- **thumbnail**: A small picture drawn by the client for a catalog item, CAS part, Sim, household or lot. ([7.03](7.03-thumbnails-gallery.md))
- **`thumbnails.package`**: A package of pre-made JPEG thumbnails shipped with the game and with each pack; 12 in this install. ([7.03](7.03-thumbnails-gallery.md))
- **tick**: The game's unit of time: one millisecond of game time; 1,500 ticks make one sim minute. ([1.01](1.01-time-scheduling-loading.md))
- **time block**: One entry of a forecast's weather_event_time_blocks: a start hour and the weighted events that may begin while it is in force. ([2.04](2.04-weather-seasons-ground.md))
- **time debt**: Per-Sim record of how far the server has run ahead or the client has lagged; repaid by sleeping longer at a looping animation. ([3.06](3.06-animation.md))
- **time jump**: The rule for loading a saved situation after time has passed: disallow, allow, simulate or gig based. ([4.01](4.01-situations-npcs.md))
- **time overhead**: An affordance's tuned length in Sim minutes for scoring; higher values make distance matter less. ([3.04](3.04-autonomy.md))
- **time passage fixup**: The rule a commodity uses to catch up when its Sim is instantiated: decay for the elapsed time, jump to the auto-satisfy curve, or do nothing. ([3.03](3.03-needs-statistics.md))
- **time slice**: The real-time budget per frame for advancing the sim timeline (33 ms as tuned); work past it waits for the next frame. ([1.01](1.01-time-scheduling-loading.md))
- **timed aspiration**: A TimedAspiration that runs for a time span or weekly schedule with complete, failure and cancel loots. ([3.07](3.07-personality-feelings.md))
- **timed aspiration loot**: The loot key that activates, deactivates or adds objectives to a timed aspiration, or moves it in or out of the suggested list. ([3.07](3.07-personality-feelings.md))
- **timed buff commodity**: The hidden runtime commodity a timed buff owns: it starts at the buff's duration, drains one point per Sim minute and removes the buff at 0. ([3.03](3.03-needs-statistics.md))
- **timed-trigger unit**: The unit of `trigger_time`, read through `interval_in_real_seconds`: 1,000 game ticks, two thirds of a Sim minute. ([2.02](2.02-objects-states-wear.md))
- **TimedStateChange**: A state component rule that moves a state on after a timed delay, in units of 1,000 ticks (40 Sim seconds). ([2.02](2.02-objects-states-wear.md))
- **tip group**: A TUTORIAL_TIP_GROUP instance listing tips that must all (or any) be satisfied before dependent tips may show. ([7.01](7.01-ui-dialogs-tutorials.md))
- **TNS**: The code's name for a notification: the message card in the corner of the screen (UiDialogNotification), sent on the op stream. ([7.01](7.01-ui-dialogs-tutorials.md))
- **TONE**: Skin tone resource (type 0x0354796A): three texture layers, age-gender overlays, hue, saturation, opacity, tags and a type (warm, neutral, cool, misc). ([8.03](8.03-sim-cas-files.md))
- **TOOL path**: The p attribute on resource-key values: the developer source file the key was built from; the game never reads it. ([8.02](8.02-tuning-formats.md))
- **tooltip test**: A test with a tuned tooltip; when it is the reason an option fails, the option is shown greyed out instead of hidden. ([0.04](0.04-tests-loot-effects.md))
- **topic**: A short conversation memory on a Sim with a score bonus and a relevancy that runs down per interaction or by time. ([3.08](3.08-relationships-socials.md))
- **townie**: A non-played Sim, usually in a homeless household that has a home world but no lot. ([4.02](4.02-story-progression-townies.md))
- **TrackDiagnosticAction**: Interaction element that records an exam or treatment and applies the illness's examination or treatment loots. ([3.13](3.13-health-luck-fame.md))
- **tracker LOD threshold**: The lowest Sim info LOD at which a tracker is kept (_tracker_lod_threshold, default BACKGROUND). ([1.03](1.03-performance-lod.md))
- **tradition**: A HolidayTradition: a goal plus buffs, walk-bys, situations, drama nodes and price multipliers active during a holiday. ([4.04](4.04-events-holidays-festivals.md))
- **tradition preference**: How much a Sim cares about a tradition: DOES_NOT_CARE (x0), LIKES (x1) or LOVES (x2) on goal points. ([4.04](4.04-events-holidays-festivals.md))
- **TraditionTest**: A test that checks the active traditions against a white or black list; fixed in result when EP05 is missing. ([4.04](4.04-events-holidays-festivals.md))
- **Trailblazer**: Fame perk whose holder's everyday outfit may be copied (12% per roll) by situation Sims on the lot. ([3.13](3.13-health-luck-fame.md))
- **Trained out**: The end state of a habit: the pet gains trait_DisciplinedOut_* and stops misbehaving that way unless it is Vengeful. ([3.12](3.12-pets-horses.md))
- **Training command**: One of eight dog tricks (Sit, Speak, LieDown, RollOver, Shake, PlayDead, Fetch, Heel) learned when its progress commodity reaches 100. ([3.12](3.12-pets-horses.md))
- **trait**: A Trait instance a Sim owns; it acts mostly through the buffs it adds, its buff replacements, excluded moods, mixers and whim set. ([3.07](3.07-personality-feelings.md))
- **trait picker**: An interaction that lists traits in a picker dialog and adds or removes the chosen ones; six classes exist, two have live instances. ([3.07](3.07-personality-feelings.md))
- **trait preference**: content_score.trait_preference: points added to a social's content score when the actor has a listed trait. ([3.07](3.07-personality-feelings.md))
- **trait statistic**: A TraitStatistic, a statistic that moves with periodic tests and unlocks, risks or locks a lifestyle trait by thresholds. ([3.07](3.07-personality-feelings.md))
- **trait type**: TraitType of a trait, for example PERSONALITY, HIDDEN, ASPIRATION, FEAR, LIKE or DISLIKE (36 values). ([3.07](3.07-personality-feelings.md))
- **trait-owned buff**: A buff listed in a trait's buffs or always_on_buffs, present for as long as the Sim has the trait. ([3.07](3.07-personality-feelings.md))
- **`trait_Occult_NoOccult`**: The trait added when a Sim owns no occult type besides HUMAN. ([3.11](3.11-occults.md))
- **transition**: The walk and posture changes that bring a Sim from where it is to where an interaction can run. ([3.05](3.05-interactions-postures-routing.md))
- **transition failure reason**: Why a transition failed (no destination node, no path, reservation, blocking object, slope, head clearance and others). ([3.05](3.05-interactions-postures-routing.md))
- **transition interaction**: An interaction the posture graph pushes to provide one posture change along a path, inserted NEXT with must-run-next. ([3.05](3.05-interactions-postures-routing.md))
- **transition sequence controller**: The object that plans and runs an interaction's transition for every Sim it needs. ([3.05](3.05-interactions-postures-routing.md))
- **trap placeholder**: An object tagged Func_Temple_Trap that the temple replaces at build time with a random trap object from its room's tuning. ([6.03](6.03-pack-systems.md))
- **travel**: Moving Sims to another lot: the script side sends MSG_TRAVEL_SIMS_TO_ZONE and pauses, the engine saves, tears down and loads the new lot. ([2.06](2.06-worlds-regions-travel.md))
- **travel group**: A set of Sims staying at a zone that is not their home, with a start, an optional end and a rented zone. ([2.06](2.06-worlds-regions-travel.md))
- **travel group limit**: Venue tunable capping how many travel groups may rent a zone at once (default 1). ([2.01](2.01-lots-venues-rooms.md))
- **travel interaction name**: A venue's rule for naming the interaction that travels to a lot, such as Ring Doorbell, Visit {Sim} or Go Home. ([2.01](2.01-lots-venues-rooms.md))
- **travel liability**: TravelSimLiability: the go-home liability that either sends the whole household or removes the leaving Sims on a split travel. ([2.06](2.06-worlds-regions-travel.md))
- **travel request behaviour**: The rule that decides whether a situation may start in another zone and send the household there. ([4.01](4.01-situations-npcs.md))
- **travel save**: The scratch save made when a client leaves for another lot. The game-service tier skips its save; the core tier still writes the account, the lot being left, unloaded lots' statistics and the camera, and a Sim removed alone (NPC travel, split go-home, travel to an object) is saved directly; a whole-household trip saves no Sim to the slot, its state is copied into memory at teardown. ([1.02](1.02-saves-persistence.md))
- **travel situation**: The situation created at the destination zone to carry the traveling Sims (live Situation_Invite_To). ([2.06](2.06-worlds-regions-travel.md))
- **TrayMetadata**: Protobuf header of every shared tray item (household, lot, room or part): name, creator, counts, flags and a type-specific block. ([8.03](8.03-sim-cas-files.md))
- **trend**: One of 61 topics (skill, emotional or generic) that are currently popular for videos; four are current at a time. ([4.03](4.03-groups-factions.md))
- **trend recording**: Stamping a recorded video with the trend of the celebrity, child or skill seen while recording. ([4.03](4.03-groups-factions.md))
- **trigger interaction**: The one interaction on a room's trigger object that opens the gate; every other trap interaction gives a punishment. ([6.03](6.03-pack-systems.md))
- **trigger object**: The one placed trap in a temple room whose correct interaction opens that room's gate, picked at random when the temple is built. ([6.03](6.03-pack-systems.md))
- **tunable**: A Python object that describes one tuning field: its type, default and how it is read from XML. ([0.03](0.03-tuning-system.md))
- **tunable multiplier**: A base value multiplied by every entry whose tests pass. ([0.03](0.03-tuning-system.md))
- **TunableFactory**: A tunable that produces a callable or object built from a class's FACTORY_TUNABLES. ([0.03](0.03-tuning-system.md))
- **TunableInstanceParam**: An argument factory that turns a typed id, exact name or unique name fragment into a tuning class. ([1.04](1.04-debug-cheats-telemetry.md))
- **TunablePlayAudio**: Tunable that wraps a PROPX key with an optional joint, a play-on-active-Sim-only flag and an immediate flag, and builds a PlaySound. ([7.02](7.02-audio-vfx-camera.md))
- **TunedInterval**: The value of a TunableInterval: lower_bound and upper_bound, with inclusive membership and per-call seeded random picks. ([0.03](0.03-tuning-system.md))
- **tuning**: The data records that set the game's rules and values; Python code declares the fields and tuning fills them. ([0.03](0.03-tuning-system.md))
- **tuning blueprint**: A lightweight object holding a record's tuned fields; calling it builds a live object and copies the fields onto it. ([0.03](0.03-tuning-system.md))
- **tuning dependencies cache**: A per-pack prebuilt table of which records reference which, used to know what to re-read on pack hot-load. ([0.03](0.03-tuning-system.md))
- **tuning record**: One entry of tuning: an instance record (a buff, an interaction), keyed by its type and instance id, or the module tuning of one Python module. A name is unique only within a type. ([0.01](0.01-reading-guide.md))
- **turn**: One loop of a phase animation; a phase finishes after its tuned number of turns, or when a progress statistic fills. ([6.01](6.01-crafting-cooking.md))
- **tutorial tip**: A TUTORIAL_TIP instance: a client-shown hint with display rules and server gameplay (buffs, loots, restricted actions, a test that completes it). ([7.01](7.01-ui-dialogs-tutorials.md))
- **type id**: The 32-bit part of a resource key that says what format a resource is. Tuning type ids are the FNV-1 32 hash of the type's file extension. ([8.01](8.01-package-files.md))
## U

- **`ui_response`**: A tuned extra button on a dialog, with a sort order, an answer id, a client UI request or command, and optional loots applied when it is chosen. ([7.01](7.01-ui-dialogs-tutorials.md))
- **Unavailable channel**: A radio station state that a stereo's tuning hides from its station picker, such as the prom reward station on every ordinary stereo. ([7.02](7.02-audio-vfx-camera.md))
- **unclaimed craftable**: A fridge snack that is destroyed, with its price refunded, if it is still where it was made when the eating interaction ends. ([6.01](6.01-crafting-cooking.md))
- **UNDEFINED weather type**: WeatherType 10; the only weather type current when no weather service exists. ([2.04](2.04-weather-seasons-ground.md))
- **unfinished business**: A global aspiration whose objectives loot adds and removes; its track and statistic belong to EP17 (Life & Death), not installed. ([3.07](3.07-personality-feelings.md))
- **unfulfilled index**: The list number (0 to 39) a request sits in: 0 or 20 for explicit or open, plus twice the priority, plus 1 unless elevated. ([4.01](4.01-situations-npcs.md))
- **unidirectional**: Held on one side of a relationship only, such as sentiments, knowledge and the Widow bit. ([3.08](3.08-relationships-socials.md))
- **uninstantiated zone**: A lot that is not loaded but whose record was opened (home lot, lots where household Sims are); it saves only its lot statistics. ([1.02](1.02-saves-persistence.md))
- **unique situation**: A situation type with _is_unique set; a second instance is refused while one runs. ([4.01](4.01-situations-npcs.md))
- **untyped command**: A decorator with no command_type; it takes the default, DebugOnly. ([1.04](1.04-debug-cheats-telemetry.md))
- **urgency**: A notification field sent as criticality: DEFAULT or URGENT. ([7.01](7.01-ui-dialogs-tutorials.md))
- **urgency curve (ad_data)**: The tuned curve that maps a need's value to how much a Sim wants it; used as tuned, linearly interpolated. ([3.04](3.04-autonomy.md))
- **urnstone**: The urn or tombstone object that stores a dead Sim; the ghost source picks one and walks its ghost during the allowed night window. ([3.11](3.11-occults.md), [4.01](4.01-situations-npcs.md))
- **usage penalty**: A portal cost that rises each time a Sim uses the portal, so other Sims spread to other doors or stairs. ([3.05](3.05-interactions-postures-routing.md))
- **use ingredients**: The recipe picker choice that makes a craft consume fridge or inventory ingredients; unticked, none are used and the full ingredient surcharge is charged. ([6.01](6.01-crafting-cooking.md))
- **UserAccountDataTypeEnum**: Types of per-account data kept outside the save: EVENTS, REWARDS, PIVOTAL_MOMENTS, GAMEPLAY_VALUES. ([1.02](1.02-saves-persistence.md))
- **utility**: Power or water, tracked as a lot commodity that use drains and production fills; billed or sold at 0.6 Simoleons a unit live. ([5.01](5.01-money-bills-rewards.md))
- **UV set**: A per-vertex texture coordinate pair; DMAPs are sampled at a mesh's second UV set. ([3.02](3.02-cas-sculpting-parts.md))
## V

- **vacation**: The default travel group type: a stay at a rented lot, extendable for the lot's daily price. ([2.06](2.06-worlds-regions-travel.md))
- **valedictorian**: The one graduate a ceremony honours, chosen at random among NPCs if none is set. ([3.10](3.10-skills-careers-school.md))
- **value of service**: The vet buff a pet owner gets after the bill, picked from the markup and the vet's Veterinarian skill. ([5.02](5.02-businesses.md))
- **variable venue**: A venue whose variable_venues tuning lets civic policies or events switch it between sub-venues. ([2.01](2.01-lots-venues-rooms.md))
- **variant**: A tunable offering several named options, of which the tuning picks one. ([0.03](0.03-tuning-system.md))
- **vehicle**: Inventory object with a vehicle component that a Sim deploys, rides and puts away. ([2.06](2.06-worlds-regions-travel.md))
- **venue**: Tuning record that says what kind of place a lot is (house, bar, park, rental) and names its zone director, hidden lot traits and NPC rules. ([2.01](2.01-lots-venues-rooms.md))
- **venue civic policy**: A civic policy whose enactment switches a variable venue to its sub-venue. ([2.01](2.01-lots-venues-rooms.md))
- **venue cleanup**: Module-tuned actions that repair, clean and bin objects when a household visits a lot it does not own. ([2.01](2.01-lots-venues-rooms.md))
- **venue eligibility**: Whether a lot meets its venue's required and forbidden objects; decided natively. ([2.01](2.01-lots-venues-rooms.md))
- **venue event**: A drama node scheduled for a lot that can override its zone director and switch its sub-venue for a while. ([2.01](2.01-lots-venues-rooms.md))
- **venue proxy director**: A zone director class built at runtime from a proxy director (such as a career event's) plus the active venue's own director. ([2.01](2.01-lots-venues-rooms.md))
- **venue type**: The VenueTypes enum on a venue (STANDARD, RESIDENTIAL, RENTAL, VET_CLINIC, MULTI_UNIT and others) that code tests to classify a lot. ([2.01](2.01-lots-venues-rooms.md))
- **vertex id**: GEOM vertex attribute with usage 10: a stable number per head vertex that a BGEO addresses. ([3.02](3.02-cas-sculpting-parts.md))
- **VetBucks**: The perk currency of vet clinics, earned per billed treatment and spent on 10 clinic perks. ([5.02](5.02-businesses.md))
- **VFX state**: An internal state index of a running effect, switched with VFX_SET_STATE (202) without restarting the effect. ([7.02](7.02-audio-vfx-camera.md))
- **VFXMask**: 23-bit flag set the client uses to choose effect variants for the active Sim; built from trait vfx_mask flags. ([7.02](7.02-audio-vfx-camera.md))
- **ViewUpdate**: The message (MSG_OBJECTS_VIEW_UPDATE, id 11) that carries one tick's operations to the client, grouped into entries per object. ([0.02](0.02-architecture.md))
- **virtual actor**: An ASM actor bound to one part of a multi-part object rather than to a whole object. ([3.06](3.06-animation.md))
- **virtual neighbourhood**: The kingdom neighbourhood assigned by loot to a Sim that has no home zone. ([6.03](6.03-pack-systems.md))
- **visible queue cap**: `max_interactions`, the number of interactions (running one included) the pie menu lets the player queue; 6 for Sims. ([3.05](3.05-interactions-postures-routing.md))
- **visitation rights**: A venue flag (home lots) under which visitors must be greeted before they come in. ([4.01](4.01-situations-npcs.md))
- **visual type**: A notification field: INFORMATION, SPEECH (a speech-bubble card) or SPECIAL_MOMENT. ([7.01](7.01-ui-dialogs-tutorials.md))
- **VisualQuality preset**: The graphics preset (Low, LowMedium, Medium, High, Ultra, or Custom) that sets the per-feature quality options in GraphicsRules.sgr. ([1.03](1.03-performance-lod.md))
- **voice effect**: A per-Sim 64-bit voice filter picked from the highest-priority trait request, such as ghostvox or reaper. ([7.02](7.02-audio-vfx-camera.md))
- **voice suffix override**: A per-object map from SuffixType to a 32-bit hash that changes which sound variant the client picks. ([7.02](7.02-audio-vfx-camera.md))
- **voting week**: The weekly window from Friday 08:00 to Monday 18:00 in which votes count; it closes with one enact and any repeals. ([2.07](2.07-neighbourhood-systems.md))
## W

- **wading depth**: The water depth from which a Sim of a given species and age starts wading. ([2.03](2.03-build-buy-placement.md))
- **wading interval**: Water depth range (lower to upper bound) in which a Sim wades; past the upper bound it may only swim, and with no interval it may not enter ocean water. ([2.06](2.06-worlds-regions-travel.md))
- **waiting customer cap**: The number of waiting vet customer groups, set by the exam-table count, below which new groups keep spawning past the desired count. ([5.02](5.02-businesses.md))
- **walk nodes**: Attractor objects a walk-dog situation visits in angular order around their centre. ([4.01](4.01-situations-npcs.md))
- **walk style**: The locomotion style a Sim uses on a route: walk, jog, a slow short-distance walk, mood and occult variants. ([3.05](3.05-interactions-postures-routing.md))
- **walk-by**: An ambient situation in which an NPC passes through, lingers, socialises or rings the doorbell. ([4.01](4.01-situations-npcs.md))
- **walk-by social**: A conversation the ambient service starts between two free walk-by Sims within range and view. ([4.01](4.01-situations-npcs.md))
- **wall object padding**: The forward offset (default 0.25 m) used to test reachability of an object placed against a wall. ([2.03](2.03-build-buy-placement.md))
- **wall-clock timeline**: A second timeline that runs in real time, used by real-time alarms; it has no per-frame time budget. ([1.01](1.01-time-scheduling-loading.md))
- **waypoint generator**: Tuning that produces the points a jogging, pacing or wandering interaction routes through. ([3.05](3.05-interactions-postures-routing.md))
- **waypoint interaction**: An interaction that walks the Sim through points from a waypoint generator in a loop: jogging, pacing, swimming laps, wandering. ([3.05](3.05-interactions-postures-routing.md))
- **waypoint stitching**: Joining several waypoints into one planned route instead of planning one route per waypoint. ([3.05](3.05-interactions-postures-routing.md))
- **weakness points**: VampireWeaknessBucks earned at levels 4, 8, 12 and 16 and spent on weakness perks. ([3.11](3.11-occults.md))
- **weather channel**: One weather quantity sent to the client as a ramp: rain, snow, a cloud type, wind, thunder, lightning, temperature, wet ground, snow cover, frost, ice and others, each with a numeric id. ([2.04](2.04-weather-seasons-ground.md))
- **weather event**: A WeatherEvent instance: target ranges, delays and rates for rain or snow, clouds, wind, thunder and lightning, plus one temperature word. ([2.04](2.04-weather-seasons-ground.md))
- **weather service**: WeatherService: the zone service that draws forecasts, ramps weather channels, derives ground cover and sets weather types; registered only when EP05 or EP10 is available. ([2.04](2.04-weather-seasons-ground.md))
- **weather type**: A WeatherType value (temperatures, AnyRain, Rain_Storm, High_Snow_Accumulation, Windy and others) that tests and weather-aware objects react to. ([2.04](2.04-weather-seasons-ground.md))
- **weather-aware component**: WeatherAwareComponent: an object's start and end loots per weather type, inside, outside or anywhere, plus lightning and umbrella hooks. ([2.04](2.04-weather-seasons-ground.md))
- **WeatherElementTuple**: A ramp of one weather channel: start value and time, end value and time, interpolated linearly by the client. ([2.04](2.04-weather-seasons-ground.md))
- **weekly schedule**: A WeeklySchedule: a set of schedule entries that fires a callback at each entry's start time every week. ([1.01](1.01-time-scheduling-loading.md))
- **weight money multiplier**: Simoleons added to a fish's value per kilogram of its weight. ([6.02](6.02-gardening-fishing-collecting.md))
- **welcome wagon**: The one-off NPC-hosted visit of neighbours to a newly moved-in household, scheduled by NPCHostedSituationService. ([4.01](4.01-situations-npcs.md))
- **werebies**: commodity_WerewolfCreation_Werebies, the first turning stage after a bite, about 23.3 hours. ([3.11](3.11-occults.md))
- **werewolf pack**: One of two GP12 packs, each with a trait, leader and member traits and a ranked standing statistic. ([3.11](3.11-occults.md))
- **wet ground**: The RAIN_ACCUMULATION ground-cover channel: builds while it rains, dries at a temperature rate. ([2.04](2.04-weather-seasons-ground.md))
- **whim**: The game's name for a want: a situation goal shown in a want slot that pays satisfaction points when completed. ([3.07](3.07-personality-feelings.md))
- **whim set**: A weighted list of whims that feeds the want slots: an ObjectivelessWhimSet with a fixed priority or an AspirationWhimSet switched on by objectives. ([3.07](3.07-personality-feelings.md))
- **whim slot**: One of the four want slots: LONG_TERM, SHORT_TERM, REACTIONARY and CONFRONTATION. ([3.07](3.07-personality-feelings.md))
- **wild plant**: A plant of Wild quality: needs no care, never evolves, grows and fruits twice as fast, and gives fruit worth 10 percent of catalog value. ([6.02](6.02-gardening-fishing-collecting.md))
- **wildlife encounter**: A tagged world object that a scheduling walk-by director sets active or inactive once a day by chance, under a cap per wildlife group. ([4.01](4.01-situations-npcs.md))
- **wildlife encounter group**: One of seven kinds of wildlife (hornet, bat, centipede, denkimushi, kodama, firefly, onibi) whose active objects share a cap. ([4.01](4.01-situations-npcs.md))
- **will**: An EP17 record of a Sim's or household's wishes at death: heirlooms, burial, funeral activities, money split and dependents. ([3.09](3.09-life-cycle.md))
- **wind speed effect**: WindSpeedEffect: a client state change setting an object's spin speed (OFF, NORMAL, FAST) and transition speed. ([2.04](2.04-weather-seasons-ground.md))
- **window frost**: The WINDOW_FROST channel: builds at Freezing, melts at every other temperature. ([2.04](2.04-weather-seasons-ground.md))
- **WingTuning**: EP19 module tuning for when fairies take wings out or put them away while routing. ([3.11](3.11-occults.md))
- **wisp**: An EP19 light that travels between enchanted plants on a schedule; inactive without EP19. ([6.02](6.02-gardening-fishing-collecting.md))
- **work performance**: A statistic per career, from -100 to 100, that drives promotion, demotion and firing. ([3.10](3.10-skills-careers-school.md))
- **work request**: What a Sim asks the master controller for: an interaction or transition plus the other Sims it needs. ([4.02](4.02-story-progression-townies.md))
- **world**: In code, one world file, which is one street; a zone's world_id is its open street id. ([2.06](2.06-worlds-regions-travel.md))
- **world description**: Catalog id for a world file; Street.WORLD_DESCRIPTION_TUNING_MAP turns it into the street record. ([2.06](2.06-worlds-regions-travel.md))
## X

- **x index**: The number of a shared node; a pack's indices start at its pack id times 1,000,000 so that files never collide. ([8.02](8.02-tuning-formats.md))
## Y

- **yard sale**: A player-run sale from a sales table that keeps a target number of NPC customer situations topped up. ([4.01](4.01-situations-npcs.md))
## Z

- **zone**: One lot slot in a world (a lot or a plex unit) with its own saved objects, owner, statistics and settings; when loaded it runs together with its open street, and only one zone runs at a time. ([1.01](1.01-time-scheduling-loading.md), [2.01](2.01-lots-venues-rooms.md))
- **zone director**: The per-lot controller a venue names: it runs shifts, background situations, arrivals, lot preparation and cleanups, and on load decides whether each saved or arriving Sim keeps their situation, starts again or is sent home. ([1.01](1.01-time-scheduling-loading.md), [2.01](2.01-lots-venues-rooms.md))
- **zone director request**: A (type, director) pair filed with the venue service; the sorted list's first entry becomes the zone director. ([2.01](2.01-lots-venues-rooms.md))
- **zone fixup**: The venue behaviour applied to leftover non-resident NPCs when time passed or the household changed since the save. ([2.01](2.01-lots-venues-rooms.md))
- **zone modifier**: Tuning record that applies loots, schedules, statistic changes and situation rules to a lot while it is active. ([2.01](2.01-lots-venues-rooms.md))
- **zone modifier display info**: USER_INTERFACE_INFO record holding a zone modifier's icon, name, description and trait or challenge type. ([2.01](2.01-lots-venues-rooms.md))
- **zone service**: A service built fresh for each loaded zone (one lot visit) and torn down when the zone unloads, such as the object manager, situations and fire; 50 in the code. ([0.02](0.02-architecture.md), [1.01](1.01-time-scheduling-loading.md))
- **zone spin-up**: The ordered list of states run when a lot loads, from fixing Sim infos and spawning Sims to restoring interactions and preroll autonomy. ([1.01](1.01-time-scheduling-loading.md))
- **zone state**: The stage a zone is in, from ZONE_INIT (0) through CLIENT_CONNECTED and HITTING_THEIR_MARKS to RUNNING (6) and SHUTDOWN_STARTED (7); each change adds exactly 1. ([1.01](1.01-time-scheduling-loading.md))
- **ZoneObjectData**: Type 0x00000006, instance equal to the zone id: one lot's architecture blobs and object lists. ([8.04](8.04-save-file-format.md))
